Erie County Court of Common Pleas: Complete Guide (2025)

Essential Information

Address: courthouse" class="internal-link" title="Erie County Courthouse">Erie County Courthouse, 323 Columbus Ave #3, Sandusky, OH 44870, United States
Phone: (419) 627-7731
Website: https://www.eriecounty.oh.gov/CommonPleasCourt.aspx

Hours of Operation

  • Monday-Friday: 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM
  • Saturday-Sunday: Closed

What is the Erie County Court of Common Pleas?

The Erie County Court of Common Pleas serves as the primary judicial authority in Erie County, Ohio, handling major civil and criminal cases. Operating as part of Ohio's judicial system, this court provides essential legal services to residents and businesses throughout the county.

Court Divisions and Their Functions

General Division

The General Division handles both civil litigation and criminal cases that don't fall under specialized divisions. This includes:

  • Personal injury claims
  • Contract disputes
  • Felony criminal cases
  • Property disputes

Domestic Relations Division

Specializing in family matters, this division oversees:

  • Divorce proceedings
  • Child custody determinations
  • Child support calculations and enforcement
  • Domestic violence protection orders

Juvenile Division

Focusing on cases involving minors, this division handles:

  • Juvenile delinquency cases
  • Child dependency and neglect matters
  • Status offenses
  • Adoptions

Probate Division

Managing matters related to estates and guardianships, this division oversees:

  • Will validation
  • Estate administration
  • Trust management
  • Guardianships for minors and incapacitated adults

How to Search Erie County Court Records

Online Record Search Options

Erie County offers comprehensive online access to court records. To conduct a search:

  1. Visit the Erie County Clerk of Courts website
  2. Select the appropriate record type (criminal, civil, etc.)
  3. Enter search criteria (case number, party name, or date range)
  4. Review the results and access available documents

Types of Available Records

  • Civil Case Records: Lawsuits, judgments, and filings
  • Criminal Records: Charges, dispositions, and sentencing information
  • Domestic Relations Records: Divorce and custody proceedings
  • Probate Records: Wills, estates, and guardianships

Erie County Clerk of Courts: Your Records Resource

Role and Responsibilities

The Erie County Clerk of Courts serves as the official custodian of all court records, responsible for:

  • Maintaining accurate court files
  • Processing legal documents
  • Collecting court fees and fines
  • Providing public access to records

Contact Information

The Clerk's office can assist with record requests, filing questions, and general court information through multiple channels:

  • Phone: (419) 627-7731
  • Email: Available on official website
  • In-person: Erie County Courthouse during regular business hours

Understanding the Daily Court Schedule

How to Access the Daily Docket

The daily court schedule (docket) provides crucial information about upcoming court proceedings. Access options include:

  • Online: View the daily schedule on the court's official website
  • In-person: Check the bulletin boards in the courthouse lobby

What's Included in the Court Schedule

Each daily schedule contains:

  • Case numbers and party names
  • Assigned courtrooms and judges
  • Scheduled hearing times
  • Case types and brief descriptions

Navigating the Erie County Courthouse

Finding Your Courtroom

The Erie County Courthouse houses multiple courtrooms across several floors. To find your assigned courtroom:

  1. Check your hearing notice for the courtroom number
  2. Consult the directory in the main lobby
  3. Follow posted signs throughout the building
  4. Ask security personnel for directions if needed

Security Procedures

When visiting the courthouse, be prepared for:

  • Security screening upon entry (metal detectors)
  • ID verification
  • Prohibited items restrictions (weapons, recording devices)
  • COVID-19 safety protocols (as applicable)

Frequently Asked Questions

What types of cases does the Erie County Court of Common Pleas handle?

The court handles felony criminal cases, major civil litigation (claims exceeding $15,000), domestic relations matters, juvenile proceedings, and probate issues.

How can I get copies of court records?

Court records can be obtained through the Clerk of Courts office either in person, by mail request, or through the online portal for certain document types.

Do I need an attorney to file a case?

While you have the right to represent yourself (pro se), the court strongly recommends legal representation for most matters due to the complexity of legal procedures.

How are judges assigned to cases?

Cases are typically assigned to judges through a random selection process to ensure fairness and equal distribution of caseloads.

Is there parking available at the courthouse?

Yes, public parking is available in designated areas around the courthouse, including both metered street parking and nearby public lots.
